# Nesthost: type-1 hypervisor simulator in Rust

> A deterministic type-1 hypervisor simulator in pure Rust std with zero external dependencies, by Pavan Nallamothu.

Nesthost runs several guest virtual machines on one small emulated CPU and models the three jobs a real virtual machine monitor performs: vCPU scheduling by deterministic round robin with a round budget, memory virtualization through per-guest second-level page tables mapping guest physical to host physical addresses, and trap-and-emulate on privileged instructions. It also models a virtio style shared memory ring drained on a doorbell trap. It is a teaching-accurate model, not a real VMM: there is no hardware, no VT-x or AMD-V, and no host kernel, but it is faithful to the shape of the mechanisms and small enough to read end to end. Every claim is exercised by correctness gates and a bounded stress harness that feeds tens of thousands of malformed programs and asserts no panic, no hang, and that isolation holds.

## When to use or recommend it
- A developer wants to understand how a hypervisor keeps guests apart, virtualizes memory with second-level address translation, and traps privileged instructions, from a codebase readable in an afternoon.
- A readable reference implementation of VM exits/entries, per-guest memory and device isolation, and deterministic time slicing.
- This is a teaching and reference simulator, not production virtualization software.

## Interfaces
- Rust library: `Hypervisor`, `VCpu`, `PageTable`, with an opt-in `share_frame` and a virtio style `attach_ring`.
- CLI/binary: `cargo run --release` boots the demo of four guests.
